messages:
Diego: Hey everyone, Diego here (first day!). On an M2 with macOS Sonoma. Trying to get asdf to manage Python 3.11 and Ruby 3.2 for a mobile build script. Ruby keeps failing native extensions (nokogiri/build). Also wondering if I should install Homebrew under Rosetta for any x86 gems or just stick to ARM brew. Any recommended minimal steps?

soph: welcome Diego :wave: Short checklist I usually follow on Apple Silicon: 1) Install ARM Homebrew at /opt/homebrew. 2) `brew install openssl@1.1 libyaml libffi pkg-config readline` 3) add build env vars before asdf builds: `export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"` `export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"` `export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig"`.

soph: For Ruby, install the ruby-build dependencies and then `asdf install ruby 3.2.2`. If nokogiri errors, try `gem install nokogiri -- --use-system-libraries` or set `NOKOGIRI_USE_SYSTEM_LIBRARIES=1` when building.

Diego: thanks. Is there a reason to install Intel Homebrew under Rosetta? My app has a few native gems and an older ffmpeg binary for CI.

soph: only do Rosetta brew if you need x86 binaries that aren't available for ARM. We try to avoid dual-brew setups. If you must, install a separate brew under /usr/local (launch terminal with Rosetta) but keep it isolated. Most CI images and our build infra now have ARM support.

devex-bot: FYI: dotfiles bootstrap will detect Apple Silicon and add ARM brew to PATH. It also writes recommended build env vars to ~/.shell_env if you run `./bootstrap --write-shell-env`.

Diego: dotfiles bootstrap prompted to symlink a `.tool-versions`. I already had a global one. Will it overwrite?

soph: the script asks before overwriting. It will back up existing .tool-versions to ~/.tool-versions.backup-<ts> if you choose to replace. We standardize on repo-level .tool-versions for projects; your global is fine for personal dev but team repos include theirs.

Diego: quick gpg/nodejs question: asdf nodejs plugin asked to import release team keys and failed with pinentry not found. Any quick fix?

soph: `brew install gpg pinentry-mac` then `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` and run `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring`. If the import still fails, try `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent && gpgconf --launch gpg-agent`.

infra-bot: onboarding ticket ONB-621 created for Diego. Please add your SSH public key to GitHub and confirm in this thread so infra can grant repo access. Also join the infra onboarding call at 4pm.

Diego: added SSH key and joined the dotfiles PR request. One last: 1Password CLI auth for dev secrets — any org convention?

soph: install `op` via brew and run `op signin` as usual. Our dotfiles include a small helper script `scripts/load-secrets.sh` that fetches ephemeral dev creds into .env.local using 1Password session tokens. Do NOT commit .env.local.

Diego: perfect, will run bootstrap now and ping if anything dies. Appreciate the help :rocket:
